newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Amanah introduces Islamic factoring.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Amanah introduces Islamic factoring.

text.p: Amanah Factors Sdn Bhd said on Thursday it was starting Islamic factoring services to serve a niche in the fast-growing Malaysian market.
Amanah said in a statement that it would ensure compliance for the services with Islamic law by making several structural modifications.
These include removing all elements of interest payment and ensuring invoices and debts would involve transactions for the supply of goods and services sanctioned under Islamic law.
Amanah is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Komplek Kewangan Malaysia Bhd, itself a unit of Malaysia's state-owned fund Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB).
Malaysia's total factoring volume grew at an annual rate of 30 percent in the last five years to 7.5 billion ringgit in 1996.

Factoring is a financial instrument which enables clients to raise funds by selling their invoices to a factoring company. Under conventional factoring, the factoring company would advance up to 80 percent of the invoice's value factored by the client.

Amanah said its current client list comprises companies and entrepreneurs who are suppliers to the government and established companies such as power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Malaysian Airline System Bhd.
